## A new workspace layout, rebuilt views, and one window per workspace on desktop

### New Features

  * A new workspace layout: an app bar for Work, Team, Chat, Inbox, and Auto, plus a side panel you can collapse and resize.
  * Views are rebuilt. Save favorites, combine or exclude filters, and filter by agent status or "Me and my agents".
  * Change an Issue's status or assignee right from the Work sidebar.
  * On desktop, each workspace opens in its own window.
  * Set up a WeCom bot by scanning a QR code, and see the agent's progress while it replies.
  * Qoder Cloud Agents supports chat, quick create, and Issue attachments, and shows Qoder credits for each run.
  * Run tasks on ZCode.
  * Send extra instructions to a running Pi agent. Pi also loads the skills Multica installs.
  * Limit how many tasks a runtime runs at once.
  * Manage workflows from the CLI.
  * See Hermes tokens and cost while a run is in progress.
  * Resolved threads show their conclusion, so agents skip settled discussions.

### Improvements

  * Multica has a refreshed logo, icons, and colors.
  * The agent list has search again, and agent settings open from more places.
  * Empty pages share one look and suggest a next step.
  * Attachment previews have a pager below the file.
  * Skills can include up to 512 files, and failed imports show the real reason.
  * Prices are updated for MiniMax-M3, Cursor, and GPT-5.6.
  * Agents use one PR per Issue by default, and sub-Issue runs read the parent Issue.
  * Traditional Chinese uses "AI 代理" for agents.
  * The Autopilot Edit button now sits next to Run now.

### Bug Fixes

  * After a comment joins a queued run, replies in that thread still reach the right agent.
  * The floating chat (Cmd+J) no longer opens blank.
  * Lark shows binding and message checks separately.
  * Telegram private chats keep @bot in your text.
  * CLI attachment paths keep special characters, and repo checkout warns when it uses an old cache.
  * Agents see skill edits and the right skill names.
  * Tasks recover after a daemon restart, and Claude runs no longer hang at the end.
  * Onboarding counts computers correctly, and creating an agent works on narrow screens.
  * Codex models from the new catalog no longer start their own subagents.
  * Custom runtime configurations can be deleted again.
  * Hermes shows the real reason a run failed.
  * Quick create assigns the agent or squad you picked.
  * Clearing an advanced filter value no longer breaks the list.
  * The Auto nav item no longer shows a red dot you can't clear.
  * Devin lists models when you use an API key.
  * An older cancelled run no longer marks PR checks as failed.
  * The current release highlight on the changelog timeline is no longer cut off.
  * Settings search hides notification settings that aren't available.
  * Selected tabs no longer look outlined in dark mode.

# Changelog

New updates and improvements to Multica.

v0.4.16 July 31, 2026

## One-click next steps, link cards, and steadier agents

### New Features

  * Chat replies now suggest follow-up steps you can send with one click.
  * Save an agent and a prompt once, then run it from any Issue's sidebar.
  * Pasted Issue and project links now show as cards instead of raw URLs.
  * Right-click any inbox notification to mark it unread and come back later.
  * Give an agent an emoji avatar, and see which runtime it runs on.
  * Qoder CN is now available when you pick a runtime for an agent.

### Improvements

  * Deleting a large self-hosted workspace is now much faster.
  * Every workspace can now label agents and Skills to keep them organized.
  * Codex on Linux now uses the tools and logins already set up on that machine.
  * Built-in Skills have consistent names and take up far less of each agent run.
  * Dimmed text across Multica is now solid and readable instead of washed out.

### Bug Fixes

  * Multi-line prompts sent to Copilot on Windows no longer lose their line breaks.
  * Claude runs are less likely to stall while prompts are being sent
  * Self-hosted local runtime setup links now point users to the right addresses
  * MCP setup guidance and runtime support checks now match what the product can run
  * Execution logs now clear active-row highlights after the related work finishes


v0.3.12 May 29, 2026

## Issue Session Resume and Korean Support

### New Features

  * Agents that continue work from an Issue comment now resume the previous session instead of starting over, keeping the task context intact
  * Multica now supports Korean across the app, public site, and documentation, including Korean docs pages and localized date formatting
  * Issue pages now keep active agent work visible near the title, with a cleaner view when multiple agents are working at once
  * Agents can scan Issue discussions faster with thread previews, reply counts, and recent activity before opening the full conversation
  * OpenClaw runtimes can use the MCP setup saved on an agent, and Claude Opus 4.8 is available in model selection and usage estimates
  * Title fields now refresh safely after external updates, and markdown code no longer uses ligatures that can distort command flags

v0.3.6 May 22, 2026

## Smarter Welcome, Live Work Signals & Safer Collaboration

### New Features

  * New users now enter a guided welcome experience where Multica Helper can introduce the workspace, give a tour, or build a slide-style welcome page
  * Issue lists now show when agents are actively working, with per-Issue indicators, hover details, and a quick filter for work in progress
  * When a child Issue is finished, the parent Issue now receives a platform-generated update and can notify the right parent owner without creating loops
  * The public site now includes a Contact Sales flow with a business-email form and submission protection
  * Desktop users can navigate back and forward with macOS swipe gestures

### Improvements

  * Issue board cards are easier to scan, with cleaner rows, better truncation, and localized relative times
  * Create Issue keeps start date in the overflow menu until it is needed, leaving the main property bar less crowded
